First, with a store card you're actually selling your personal data, whereas in radio shack's case you were given no payment for giving them your information. And in turn the company also was supposed to not be able to receive payment for selling your info to other companies.

Second, in all the rewards card signup agreements they always explicitly state that they can share or sell your personal info to other companies, whereas in radio shack's case they explicitly stated the opposite by making legally binding claims that they would never share or sell your personal info for any reason at any time.
